Panel.Replaced: {name} left the panel. It is still running; right-click it in the Subsystems tab and choose Show on panel to bring it back.
Panel.PositionHint: Where the challenge panel starts at the top of the screen. Anyone can drag it by its header to a spot of their own.
Panel.NoCharacter: You need an assigned character to roll. Ask the GM to assign one.
Panel.NoGMActor: Select a token, or pick a PC under Roll as in the challenge window.
Panel.SkillGone: That check is no longer available.

Challenge.Label: Challenge
Challenge.Name: Name
Challenge.ModifierGone: That entry was deleted, so the changes were not saved.
Challenge.EndConfirm: End this challenge? The panel closes for everyone. The final state stays on the sheet.
Challenge.ResetConfirm: Return this challenge to unspent? Points, counters, rounds and reveals go back to how they were at Start.
Challenge.NotActiveGM: Another GM is running this challenge. Only the active GM can change it.
Challenge.NoPCSelected: Choose a PC to roll for.
Challenge.RollSkill: Roll {skill}, DC {dc}, for the chosen PC
Challenge.Subject: Subject
Challenge.StatLineHint: GM only. For example: Perception +12, Will +9.
Challenge.TracksPointsHint: Turn off for a subject that only holds actions.
Challenge.IndividualHint: Each PC has their own points here. A roll changes the roller's points.
Challenge.GoalHint: Reaching the goal marks the subject Complete.
Challenge.ActionGone: That action was deleted, so the changes were not saved.
Challenge.AlwaysHint: Players see this check from the start. It has no reveal control and is never a decoy.
Challenge.ActionDescriptionHint: What the action is and how players use it
Challenge.SecretHint: Rolled as a secret check, like Recall Knowledge.
Challenge.MaxPointsHint: The most this action can give in total. Blank for no limit.
Challenge.ThresholdDcHint: Applies while the threshold is reached: to this subject's checks, or to every check for a counter's threshold.
Challenge.PerRoundHint: Added when the round advances. Previous round takes it back.
Challenge.ChallengeModifiersHint: Entries for the whole challenge. A DC change applies to every check with the chosen skills, on any subject.
Challenge.ChallengeSkillsHint: Off: pick skills. The change applies to every check with those skills, on any subject.
Challenge.TrackLimits: A minimum is above its maximum, so that value was not limited.
Challenge.ReachedFollows: Reached follows the value on a track that counts both ways.
Challenge.PerPcHint: One value for each party PC. A roll changes the roller's value; a modifier changes everyone's. No thresholds or change each round.
Challenge.PcNoteHint: GM only. For example: 1 dud (forged papers), 1 only for paperwork.
Challenge.MultipleSubjectsHint: On: any number of subjects can be revealed at once, and the panel shows each revealed one. Off: revealing a subject hides every other subject, so players see one at a time. Use off for subjects taken in order, such as a chase's obstacles: revealing the next one moves the panel on in one click. Hiding a subject never reveals another.
Challenge.DisplayHint: How players see this counter on the panel. Hidden: GM-only; the eye button in Run mode can still reveal it, in the style chosen before. Auto: a bar if it has thresholds or counts both ways, else a number. Steps: filled segments, like the round counter. Track: a marker that moves along a row of slots. Steps and Track need a maximum and show as a bar without one.

infiltration.Benefit: The PCs gain the opportunity's benefit.

preparation.Subject: Preparation
preparation.Dud: Dud: this Edge Point secretly gives no benefit. Write it in the PC's Edge Points note.
preparation.Cursed: Cursed: a PC who uses this Edge Point gets a critical failure, even if they spend it after rolling a failure. Write it in the PC's Edge Points note.

BribeContact.Name: Bribe Contact
BribeContact.Description: Requires a contact (Gain Contact). The bribe is worth at least one-tenth of the Currency per additional PC (Table 10-9); doubling it grants a +2 circumstance bonus. DC: hard or very hard.

ForgeDocuments.Name: Forge Documents
ForgeDocuments.Use: The Edge Point is usable only when presenting paperwork.

GainContact.Name: Gain Contact
GainContact.Description: A Lore suited to the contact also works. DC: normal, hard or very hard.
GainContact.Use: Contact made. The PC can now Bribe Contact.
GainContact.Failure: The PC fails to make contact.
GainContact.CriticalFailure: The contact is insulted or spooked: future attempts take a –2 circumstance penalty. Several critical failures may turn the contact against the PCs.

Gossip.Name: Gossip
Gossip.Description: DC: normal, hard or very hard.
Gossip.CriticalSuccess: Inside information: +2 circumstance bonus to future preparation checks for this infiltration, for the PC and anyone they share it with.
Gossip.Success: The PC gains useful inside information for planning.
Gossip.CriticalFailure: Mistaken rumours: –2 circumstance penalty to the PC's next preparation check.

ScoutLocation.Name: Scout Location
ScoutLocation.Description: DC: normal, hard or very hard.

SecureDisguises.Name: Secure Disguises
SecureDisguises.Description: DC: normal, hard or very hard.
SecureDisguises.Use: The Edge Point is usable only to maintain a cover identity.

chase.Label: Chase
chase.Subject: Obstacle
chase.GmNotes: Chase reminders (GM Core). Obstacles are cleared in order; extra Chase Points don't carry over, and PCs who haven't acted can go on to the next obstacle. A PC who passes or can't act costs the group 1 CP: use − on the obstacle's points. The Party and Quarry counters hold obstacle numbers. Set both maximums to the number of obstacles. When the party clears an obstacle, add 1 to Party and reveal the next obstacle (that hides the cleared one). The other side moves +1 each round; nudge it by hand on hard obstacles. Chase types: Chase Down: the quarry starts 1 ahead; the party catches it on reaching its obstacle, and it escapes once past the last. Run Away: rename Quarry to Pursuers and start it at 0; the party escapes past the last obstacle or 3 ahead at the end of a round, and is caught if they reach its obstacle. Beat the Clock: hide the other side and set the round maximum to the number of obstacles. Competitive: rename Quarry to Rival and start it at 1; whoever passes the last obstacle first wins, and initiative is rolled each round. If the party is stuck on one obstacle for about 3 rounds, let them find another way. Attack rolls and spells are yours to adjudicate: apply the degree from the roll card or change points by hand.
